question: Which published claims rest on a single REPORT that nothing else confirms?
method: records with kind=wire and corroboration == 1 whose sources are all reporting types (news, blog, misc). Corroboration counts distinct publisher hosts, not URLs. Claims resting on a single PRIMARY document are listed separately below and are not counted here: a court filing is not relaying someone else's claim, it is the record, so 'only one source' means something different about it.

Officials said days of storms and flooding across Indiana had left at least seven people dead as of Sunday 16 August 2026, with floodwaters peaking in Indianapolis' White River and rains expected to ease in the state capital region and other parts of the state.

Gov. Mike Braun said he spoke with President Trump, who on Saturday 15 August 2026 approved the governor's request for a presidential emergency declaration freeing up to $5 million in federal resources for response and recovery after days of record rainfall in Indiana.

The NFL's Indianapolis Colts and the NBA's Indiana Pacers each said on Sunday 16 August 2026 that they are donating $125,000 to statewide flood relief, with the WNBA's Indiana Fever and the G League's Noblesville Boom also contributing, the money going directly to the American Red Cross.

The Indiana Department of Homeland Security listed storm-related deaths including a 4-year-old boy in Jennings County, a 58-year-old woman in Lake County, an 86-year-old woman in Porter County, a 32-year-old man in LaPorte County and a 31-year-old man in Henry County.

Christine Altman, president of the Hamilton County board of commissioners, said at a Sunday briefing that the county just north of Indianapolis escaped without any loss of life, while officials assessed whether a significant bridge damaged in the flooding could be repaired or needed complete replacement.

Indianapolis Mayor Joe Hogsett said the flooding was the worst the capital city has seen in more than 30 years, a characterisation he repeated as first responders used boats to reach residents stranded in neighbourhoods along the White River.

Liz Woods, a spokesperson for the Indiana Department of Homeland Security, said a 4-year-old boy, two men and three women were among those who had died since the storms began on 11 August 2026, a total of six at that point in the reporting.

Nearly 130,000 utility customers across Indiana remained without power by midday Sunday 16 August 2026, down from a peak of around 300,000, according to the state homeland security spokesperson and the online utility tracker PowerOutage.us.

The White River crested at more than 24 feet (7.32 meters) in the Indiana communities of Anderson and Noblesville, surpassing records set in 1913, as heavy rains caused rivers statewide to reach record levels over the past week.

By Sunday 16 August 2026 the Indiana Department of Homeland Security count had risen to a 4-year-old boy, three men and three women dead since the storms began on 11 August, spokesperson Liz Woods said, one man more than the toll given a day earlier.

A 31-year-old cyclist was found dead early Sunday 16 August 2026 in a hole that opened up on a washed-out road in Henry County, east of Indianapolis, and the county coroner said the man appears to have gone around a barricade and fallen into the collapsed road.

The Indianapolis Department of Public Works reopened the city's floodgates on Sunday 16 August 2026 after the White River peaked early that morning, urging residents to be cautious as they returned to flood-damaged neighbourhoods while emergency shelters remained open.

The National Weather Service warned that while northern parts of Indiana dried out, a cluster of storms was expected to pass through the central and southern regions later on Sunday 16 August 2026, bringing potential heavy rain, flash flooding and damaging winds.

Rita Reith, a spokesperson with the Indianapolis Fire Department, put the number of rescues at 95 people and 45 pets as of late afternoon on Saturday 15 August 2026, with dispatchers having received hundreds of calls for service throughout the day.

More than a dozen Indiana counties had declared local disasters by Saturday 15 August 2026, with much of the latest damage concentrated along river corridors running from Hamilton County into the northern Indianapolis suburbs.

Jacob Spence, director of Marion County Emergency Management, called the flooding a once-in-a-lifetime type flood, telling The Associated Press that it was an unprecedented event in which the state was setting new records.

Adm. Brad Cooper, the head of U.S. Central Command, visited the USS Abraham Lincoln on Saturday 15 August 2026 and praised its crew, calling his time aboard "awe-inspiring" in a statement shared on social media.
The Lincoln carries about 5,000 service members, deployed to the Pacific in November 2025, arrived in the Middle East in January 2026, and has been supporting the U.S. war against Iran.
The Lincoln has spent a record-setting uninterrupted period of more than 240 days at sea, against a normal U.S. military vessel deployment of about six months, CBS News reported on 16 August 2026.

Retired Adm. Mike Mullen, a former chair of the joint chiefs of staff, said on 16 August 2026 that he spoke with Cooper on Saturday evening and was told poor conditions aboard the Lincoln had been addressed and crew morale improved once sailors learned they were going home.

Rep. Don Bacon, a Nebraska Republican and retired Air Force brigadier general, said on 16 August 2026 that Congress should conduct oversight of conditions aboard the USS Abraham Lincoln and that the secretary of the Navy or the service chief should testify before lawmakers.

Acting Secretary of the Navy Hung Cao said in a post on X on Friday 14 August 2026 that the Lincoln "will return home soon as part of a planned rotation" and that a "small number of mental health cases were treated with no loss of life."

Democratic Sen. Richard Blumenthal wrote to Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth on Thursday 13 August 2026 calling for the Navy to account for conditions aboard the carrier, which he said has been deployed more than 250 days and has not come ashore in over 200 days.

Bacon said that in 1996, when the United States was not at war, he served aboard an aircraft carrier enforcing the southern no-fly zone over Iraq and that a couple of crew members jumped overboard and died by suicide during that deployment.

Family members of USS Abraham Lincoln crew told NPR in a report published 15 August 2026 that President Trump should be "ashamed" of conditions aboard the ship and that his "not nearly long enough" comment was shameful.

Cooper said in his statement that the Lincoln crew is "a strong team of high-achieving Americans" and that history will record the deployment as one of the most operationally intense and consequential of the modern era.
